q: Why is ROAS increasing while net profit is declining?

checks.what: tool: ROAS attempted or derived from its definition

answer:
Short answer
- The data agrees: product-level net ROAS (allocated) rose while net profit (P&L) fell. ROAS up but profit down because ROAS measures return per allocated ad rupee on product-attributed lines (it improved in specific products/platforms), but overall contribution margin and sales fell and P&L ad spend rose slightly — the margin loss more than wiped out the ROAS gain.

Key evidence (previous period → current period)
- Net profit (net profit, order-date P&L): ₹-35,790 → ₹-60,859 (worse by 70.0%) — Measured
- Product net ROAS (product net ROAS (allocated), allocated): 0.73x → 0.80x (+10.0%) — Measured
- Contribution margin: ₹333,755 → ₹314,280 (down; effect on net profit: −₹19,475, 78% of the net-profit change) — Measured
- Ad spend (P&L basis): ₹369,545 → ₹375,138 (up; effect on net profit: −₹5,594, 22% of the net-profit change) — Measured
- Net sales per day: ₹91,705 → ₹75,013 (down) and Return revenue per day: ₹14,252 → ₹4,138 (down) — Measured

How to read this (labels)
- Measured: ROAS rose at the product/allocation level (better return on the ad budget for the lines we allocate to products). Net profit fell because the P&L bridge shows a drop in contribution margin was the dominant negative driver, with a smaller negative contribution from slightly higher ad spend. All numbers above come from the diagnosis run and the catalogue definitions.
- Derived: The exact split of the net-profit change → ~78% from lower contribution margin, ~22% from higher ad spend (the bridge provided by the P&L composition).
- Hypothesis (plausible, not proven here): ROAS improved because sales shifted toward product(s)/placements that are more ad-efficient (diagnose flagged Meta / IG_feed and some TN shipping-state gains). Meanwhile overall sales, returns and per-order margins fell (or losses on some SKUs increased), hurting the consolidated P&L.
